project.name: jakyeamos-agent-skills
project.identity: A public, vendor-neutral magazine and workbench for prompts, skills, playbooks, setups, tools, briefs, and references that multiply useful agent work.
project.audience: People and agent developers who want to discover reusable workflow multipliers by type or use case, inspect their evidence, and adopt them deliberately across hosts.
project.core_loop: Capture a recurring workflow advantage, classify and package it as a catalog entry, validate and publish the generated browse surface, then inspect, dry-run, adopt, and maintain it deliberately.
project.north_star: A growing collection stays easy to browse and safe to adopt without duplicating inventories, destabilizing existing install paths, or turning private context and hidden side effects into product dependencies.
not_this: A claim of provider parity without trigger and behavior evidence

mvp.definition: The catalog can package and validate a small set of portable workflows and show their setup effects through dry-run or explicit apply paths.

complete_product.definition: The workbench supports a maintained, provider-neutral catalog with compatibility evidence, safe setup, lifecycle updates, and recoverable adoption across supported hosts.

outcomes.name: A workflow can be reused because its inputs, effects, triggers, and compatibility boundaries are explicit and validated.

layers.intended: Operators can adopt useful workflows without importing hidden private state or unsafe assumptions.
layers.planned: The public repository defines a catalog and setup engine with dry-run and apply modes.
layers.implemented: The repository contains portable workflow packages and setup machinery.
layers.verified: Repository docs establish the catalog scope; broad host trigger and behavior parity was not executed here.

evidence.note: Defines the Portable Agentic Workbench catalog and setup engine.
Defines repository workflow and public-scope constraints.

blockers.summary: Provider-host trigger, loaded-context, and behavior parity evidence remains incomplete.

outcomes.name: Users can inspect setup changes before applying them and retain a clear boundary between catalog evidence and host state.

layers.intended: Adoption is deliberate, recoverable, and safe for public and private environments.
layers.planned: The project explicitly supports dry-run and apply flows.
layers.implemented: Setup and validation surfaces exist in the repository.
layers.verified: No fresh host installation or rollback was performed in this bootstrap.

blockers.summary: Host-specific installation, permissions, and rollback behavior remain dependent on the operator and supported provider environments.

verified.note: Documented claims; no host installation or parity run here.

drift.summary: The reusable workflow outcome depends on provider and host trigger/behavior evidence that the public catalog alone cannot establish.

evidence.note: Defines the public setup surface without host-wide proof.
